title: The resurrection body (1 Corinthians 15:35–44)
hookLine: sown a seed, raised a plant: perishable to imperishable
tomorrow: O death, where is your sting? (1 Corinthians 15:55)

lines: WITH WHAT BODY DO THEY COME?
cards: "How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come?" That's not a skeptic's heckle from today. Paul puts it in the mouth of "some man" in a letter to the church in Corinth.
It's a fair question. If a body is buried and returns to dust, what comes back? The same knees?
The same scar? A body at eighty, or at twenty? People in Corinth seem to have found it hard to picture.
Paul's reply starts bluntly, "Thou fool," but he doesn't leave it there. He answers with something you could hold in your palm: a seed.

teach.b: First, the seed. Paul says "that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die," and "thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain." You don't plant a wheat stalk.
You plant a small dry kernel, and what comes up looks nothing like it. Yet it's the same life: what goes into the ground and what rises belong to each other. Second, God is good at bodies.
People, animals, birds and fish all have different flesh.
The sun, the moon and the stars each have their own glory, and "one star differeth from another star in glory." The God who made that much variety, Paul is saying, can make a new kind of body too.

teach.h: SOWN IN WEAKNESS, RAISED IN POWER.
teach.b: Third, the list: "It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption: It is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power." Each line is a before and an after.

teach.h: A SPIRITUAL BODY, NOT A GHOST.
teach.b: Fourth, the surprising phrase: "It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body." Not a ghost, and not a body made of fog.
Some readers take it to mean a body fully alive with God's Spirit, still a body, but no longer headed for the grave.
The creed in the Book of Common Prayer doesn't say the soul floats on; it says "the Resurrection of the body." Christians hold a hope with the same shape as the seed: real continuity, real change.

how: Christians confess the resurrection of the body in the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds, and 1 Corinthians 15 is among the readings offered for funerals.

o: a ghostly body of light that floats free of the grave
the old body put back exactly as it was before death
the body God raises, like a seed: the same life, changed

games.q: the resurrection body — tap the pairs.
p: with what body do they come?
alive with God's Spirit, not a ghost

s: Paul refuses to answer the question about bodies
he calls the asker a fool, then answers anyway, with a seed and the stars.
Paul says what's sown and what's raised look the same
you sow bare grain, not the body that shall be. same life, new form.
one star differs from another star in glory
Paul's way of saying God already makes many kinds of bodies and glories.

games.q: you're Paul. someone in Corinth asks how the dead can possibly be raised, and with what body. how do you answer?
o: point to a seed: what you sow is not what comes up.
say only the soul lives on, so bodies don't matter.
games.why: he answers with a seed. "thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain." then the list: sown in weakness, raised in power.

practice: If you have a seed handy, an apple pip or a bean, hold it in your palm; if not, picture one, small and dry, looking nothing like what it will become. Set one person you've lost beside it in your mind.
If you pray, read Paul's line slowly, sown in weakness, raised in power; if not, simply hold the seed and wonder.

wordCard.voice: The resurrection body. Paul's picture of the body raised by God: sown like a seed, perishable, and raised imperishable, a spiritual body.

orig.note: Greek: a spiritual body, Paul's phrase in 1 Corinthians 15:44.

carryVoice: Your line: sown, raised. The same life, coming up as a changed body. Until tomorrow.
